events.title: Nyquist establishes digital sampling limits
events.summary: Harry Nyquist's April 1928 AIEE paper showed that telegraph bandwidth must scale with signaling speed — the foundation of the Nyquist rate used in every analog-to-digital converter.
events.about: Nyquist proved you need at least twice the highest signal frequency to represent a waveform without ambiguity — the rule behind audio CDs, digital radio, and Shannon's later information theory. Every microphone, modem, and scope samples because of this 1928 result.

narrative.whyChosen: The Nyquist rate is the bridge between continuous physics and discrete bits.
narrative.whyImportant: It set the minimum sample rate engineers must obey when digitizing any signal.
narrative.problemSolved: Telegraph and telephone engineers had no rigorous link between channel bandwidth and maximum signaling speed.
